scope: Fuzzing, observability, telemetry, durable workflows and streaming data systems
method: Official repository descriptions and README material checked for these sources where available; broad architecture notes only. No packages installed, REA run, source patch, build or SYLPH runtime test in this batch.

discoveries: Cargo subcommand for libFuzzer-based Rust fuzz targets.
README documents nightly Rust and LLVM sanitizer requirements and says native Windows is unsupported.
patterns: Fuzz binary parsers and protocol adapters at isolated Rust boundaries.
Preserve minimized crashing inputs as permanent regression fixtures.
overlap: Fuzzing strategy is useful; cargo-fuzz does not exercise the current TypeScript implementation.
risks: Host platform/toolchain constraints.
A Rust harness does not establish TypeScript parser safety.
validation: Use the existing TS runtime to test equivalent malformed inputs.
If Rust code is later added, run on supported Unix CI and retain corpus.

provenance: Official Grafana Loki repository README; accessed 2026-10-14.
discoveries: Horizontally scalable log aggregation with labels indexed rather than full log contents.
Official README identifies Alloy as the collection agent replacing Promtail for ongoing log collection.
patterns: Use bounded-cardinality labels such as service, environment and component.
Keep sensitive payloads and wallet data out of logs.
overlap: Would complement application logs; current registry does not establish a Loki deployment.
risks: High-cardinality labels inflate storage and query cost.
Repository states AGPL-3.0-only, requiring license review before adoption.
validation: Prototype using synthetic logs only.
Verify redaction, retention, access controls and label cardinality.

provenance: Official Grafana Tempo repository description; accessed 2026-10-14.
discoveries: Distributed tracing backend designed for high-volume traces and object-storage-based operation.
Integrates with Grafana, Prometheus and Loki for trace/metrics/log correlation.
patterns: Propagate correlation IDs across ingest, recovery and dashboard requests.
Record provider/slot span attributes without putting secrets in trace baggage.
overlap: Tracing can make existing boundaries observable without adding a second state authority.
risks: Unbounded trace attributes can expose sensitive data and create cost.
AGPL-3.0 license requires review.
validation: Use synthetic requests to verify trace continuity and redaction.
Measure sampling and retention behavior before production.

discoveries: Developer-focused performance testing with JavaScript scenarios and HTTP, WebSocket and gRPC support.
Supports thresholds and workload scenarios suitable for expressing service-level expectations.
patterns: Load test read-only dashboard and ingestion mocks with explicit thresholds.
Simulate realistic bursts and reconnect patterns, not live trades.
overlap: External test tooling; no runtime integration required.
risks: Load generation against real providers can incur cost or trigger abuse controls.
AGPL-3.0 license; extension and deployment requirements need review.
validation: Only target local or explicitly authorized staging endpoints.
Record script, thresholds, environment and result artifacts.

discoveries: Continuous profiling system for analyzing CPU and memory behavior over time.
Profiling complements request traces by identifying resource hotspots.
patterns: Profile local/staging parsers and backfills under representative synthetic load.
Compare profiles across revisions rather than relying on anecdotal latency.
overlap: Observability aid only; does not change ingestion decisions.
risks: Profiles can capture sensitive strings or identifiers.
License and deployment requirements should be checked at a pinned revision.
validation: Use non-sensitive fixtures and redact symbols/labels where needed.
Establish reproducible baselines and quantify overhead.
sources.license: Not independently verified in this review

provenance: Official Grafana Alloy repository and Loki README reference; accessed 2026-10-14.
discoveries: Grafana identifies Alloy as an observability collector/agent for gathering and forwarding telemetry.
Loki README says Alloy is the recommended successor for log collection as Promtail is feature complete.
patterns: Centralize telemetry collection configuration and apply redaction before export.
Keep collection pipeline config version-controlled.
overlap: Collector can route existing signals; it should not become a source of trading state.
risks: Collector configuration can leak data or create high-cardinality telemetry.
Licensing, supported components and upgrade path require revision-specific review.
validation: Test redaction and delivery failure behavior using synthetic data.
Pin collector version and configuration digest.
sources.license: Not independently verified in this review

provenance: Official Prometheus repository README and getting-started documentation; accessed 2026-10-14.
discoveries: Metrics system uses labeled time series, PromQL, pull-based scraping and rule evaluation.
The repository cautions that the main Prometheus codebase is a standalone server, not a supported general-purpose library.
patterns: Expose health, lag, retry, recovery coverage and execution-cost metrics with bounded labels.
Alert on SLO violations rather than raw noisy events.
overlap: Metrics export complements current state snapshots; no need to embed Prometheus into the engine.
risks: High-cardinality token/wallet labels can overwhelm storage.
Prometheus project is not intended as an embedded library.
validation: Check metric naming, cardinality and counter reset semantics.
Verify alerts against injected stale-feed and ingress-failure scenarios.

discoveries: Collector is an extensible vendor-neutral pipeline for receiving, processing and exporting telemetry.
Component availability and stability vary by distribution and individual receiver/exporter.
patterns: Separate instrumentation from backend choice through a collector boundary.
Apply filtering, batching and redaction in explicit pipeline stages.
overlap: Could export engine metrics/traces without coupling the engine to a backend.
risks: Collector components may have different stability levels.
Misconfiguration may drop signals or export sensitive payloads.
validation: Pin distro and component versions; test loss/retry behavior.
Verify no private keys, authorization headers or raw sensitive payloads enter telemetry.

provenance: Official Temporal server repository README; accessed 2026-10-14.
discoveries: Temporal server provides durable workflow execution with retries across intermittent failures.
Server repository is distinct from language SDKs used to author workflows.
patterns: For future long-running historical backfills, model idempotent work units and durable checkpoints.
Keep recovery workflows separate from live trade execution workflows.
overlap: Existing gap reconciler and checkpointing already own recovery semantics; Temporal is not justified without a concrete orchestration gap.
risks: Retries can duplicate side effects unless activities are idempotent.
Adding distributed orchestration expands operational complexity.
validation: Prototype against local test server and idempotent test activities only.
Prove retries cannot invoke signing or broadcast paths.

discoveries: NATS server is a messaging system supporting publish/subscribe and request/reply patterns.
Durability/stream semantics depend on configured NATS capabilities and deployment.
patterns: Use message IDs, explicit acknowledgements and replay-safe consumers for internal event transport.
Preserve canonical source sequence/slot metadata through transport.
overlap: Potential transport pattern only; current ingress path remains source of truth.
risks: At-most/at-least-once semantics differ and can create gaps or duplicates.
Broker availability and persistence become operational dependencies.
validation: Inject disconnect, duplicate, out-of-order and restart scenarios in an isolated harness.
Verify idempotency and checkpoint recovery before considering production.

discoveries: Redpanda is a Kafka API-compatible streaming data platform.
Its use implies broker-backed event persistence and separate operational provisioning.
patterns: Use append-only event logs and replayable consumers for analytics pipelines.
Keep source event identity and processing intent in the message envelope.
overlap: Not needed to duplicate in-process canonical ingress; relevant only for scale-out analytics.
risks: Kafka compatibility is not identical behavior for every feature.
Operational footprint and ordering/retention configuration can affect correctness.
validation: Test ordering, retention, replay and consumer offset recovery with local fixtures.
Do not route broker events directly into signing authority.

discoveries: RisingWave is a streaming database for SQL processing over continuously arriving data.
Materialized views can expose continuously updated derived results.
patterns: Build monitoring aggregates from immutable normalized events.
Track event-time versus processing-time and late-data policy explicitly.
overlap: A separate analytics layer could complement source event storage but must not replace authoritative engine state.
risks: Late or duplicated events can change aggregates.
Database consistency and recovery behavior must be tested for chosen deployment.
validation: Replay deterministic event sequences including duplicates and late arrivals.
Compare query outputs with a reference implementation.

discoveries: Materialize provides streaming SQL and incrementally maintained materialized views.
The repository is a database system rather than a drop-in library.
patterns: Derive dashboards and research aggregates from versioned event streams.
Keep time semantics and source provenance visible in derived views.
overlap: Would be an external analytical store, not an alternate execution or health authority.
risks: External system adds consistency, access-control and operational concerns.
License and product terms require review at selected version.
validation: Compare incremental results with batch recomputation on fixtures.
Exercise restart and late-event cases.
sources.license: Not independently verified in this review

provenance: Official TimescaleDB repository description and quick-start docs; accessed 2026-10-14.
discoveries: PostgreSQL extension focused on time-series and event analytics.
Hypertables and columnar storage support time-partitioned analytical workloads.
patterns: Store immutable timestamped observations and execution records with explicit source IDs.
Separate retention/aggregation policies from canonical evidence retention.
overlap: Potential storage technology, but SYLPH's current files/database layout must be assessed before introducing another datastore.
risks: Schema/index/retention errors can compromise audit completeness.
Extension compatibility and deployment version must be pinned.
validation: Test deterministic migrations, backup/restore, duplicate handling and time-zone semantics.
Reconcile stored fills and fees against canonical records.

discoveries: Current main README describes InfluxDB 3 Core, an event/time-series database built around Arrow, DataFusion and Parquet.
Repository documents versioned branches/APIs for v1, v2 and v3; compatibility is not a single interchangeable interface.
patterns: Use time-series storage for operational metrics and low-latency analytical views.
Pin server generation, write protocol and query API in deployment contracts.
overlap: Potential external store only; not an engine-state replacement.
risks: Version/API differences across branches can break ingestion assumptions.
README claims should be benchmarked against local workload and retention needs.
validation: Test write/query round trips, timestamp precision, retention and restart behavior.
Never use dashboards as authoritative fill or health evidence without reconciliation.
